slides.text: 5 rules that make Claude design like a studio
slides.sub: Ask for a deck and you get template soup. Give it rules and you get design.
The whole trick in one line. Don't ask for a presentation about X. Hand it design rules and make it obey them. Every rule after this one is a constraint worth stealing.
Say it exactly like that, one idea per slide, huge readable text, no bullet point soup. The moment a slide makes two points it makes zero.
Dark background, one bright accent, generous white space. One color choice is what separates designed from decorated. Let everything else stay quiet.

Add: at least one slide must use a simple chart or diagram instead of text. It will happily write paragraphs forever unless you force it to draw, and the drawn slide is always the one people remember.
After the first draft, go surgical. Make slide 3 more visual. Rewrite every headline under 7 words. Punchier. You're the art director now, and it takes notes better than any designer you've met.
